title: How do climate scientists make predictions?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: statement about what you think will happen in the future
depending on other factors; not certain
(informal) used to introduce the most important feature or detail to understand about something
(idiom) out of balance; not working properly or broken
(idiom) (not) considered an option or a possibility

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是BBC学英语的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Pippa. This summer is becoming one of the hottest ever with heatwaves across Europe.
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Pippa。今年夏天正成为欧洲各地热浪滚滚、史上最热的夏天之一。

sentences.en: Here in the UK, a new record for the highest June temperature was set at a sweltering 37.7°C.
sentences.zh: 在英国，6月最高气温创下了37.7摄氏度的高温纪录。

sentences.en: It seems that year after year, temperatures are going up.
sentences.zh: 似乎年复一年，气温都在不断上升。

sentences.en: In 2015, the COP21 summit agreed to limit global warming to 1.5°C, but since then research shows temperatures exceeding that, leading to warnings of catastrophic damage to Earth's life support systems.
sentences.zh: 在2015年，巴黎气候变化大会同意将全球变暖限制在1.5摄氏度以内，但自那以后，研究表明气温已经超过了这一限度，从而引发了对地球生命支持系统遭受灾难性破坏的警告。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll be discussing how hot the planet could get, using some useful new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将讨论地球可能会变得多热，并学习一些有用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find a free transcript to read along with on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到免费的节目文稿来对照阅读。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Phil.
sentences.zh: 但首先，Phil，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: Scientists monitor climate change using the Earth's energy imbalance – the difference between the solar energy entering the Earth's atmosphere and the radiation going back out into space.
sentences.zh: 科学家利用地球的能量不平衡来监测气候变化——也就是进入地球大气层的太阳能与返回太空的辐射之间的差值。

sentences.en: But which unit do scientists use for this?
sentences.zh: 但是科学家用哪个单位来测量这个呢？

sentences.en: Ooh, I know Joules is something to do with energy, so I'm going to go with c).
sentences.zh: 哦，我知道焦耳（Joules）和能量有关，所以我选 c)。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme, although careful listeners might hear the answer sooner.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们将在节目结束时揭晓答案，不过仔细听节目的听众可能会更早听到答案。

sentences.en: Ooh! Yes, exciting! So, how do scientists calculate the effects of climate change in the first place?
sentences.zh: 哦！太好了，令人兴奋！那么，科学家究竟是如何计算气候变化的影响的呢？

sentences.en: The answer is with models. Huge amounts of physical and chemical data are fed into supercomputers, which then paint pictures of possible futures on Earth.
sentences.zh: 答案是通过模型。大量的物理和化学数据输入超级计算机，然后计算机绘制出地球未来可能情况的画面。

sentences.en: But, as NASA climate scientist Kate Marvel explained to BBC World Service programme The Climate Question, nothing is certain.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如美国宇航局（NASA）气候科学家Kate Marvel向BBC世界服务部节目《气候问题》所解释的那样，没有什么事是确定的。

sentences.en: Climate models don't make predictions – they make projections.
sentences.zh: 气候模型不做预测——它们做的是预估（projections）。

sentences.en: Predictions are saying this is what will happen and a projection is conditional.
sentences.zh: 预测是说一定会发生什么，而预估是有条件的。

sentences.en: A projection is: "If we do this, then this will happen."
sentences.zh: 预估是：“如果我们这样做，就会发生这种情况。”

sentences.en: Climate models don't make predictions. Those are statements about what's likely to happen.
sentences.zh: 气候模型不做预测。那些是关于可能发生的事情的陈述。

sentences.en: Instead, they make projections about different possible futures, and these depend on many things.
sentences.zh: 相反，它们对各种可能的未来做出预估，而这些预估取决于许多因素。

sentences.en: In other words, climate models are conditional, meaning that they depend on other factors.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，气候模型是有条件的，这意味着它们取决于其他因素。

sentences.en: The main factor in climate change, of course, is human activity, especially greenhouse gas emissions.
sentences.zh: 当然，气候变化的主要因素是人类活动，尤其是温室气体排放。

sentences.en: Another influence on climate models is clouds.
sentences.zh: 对气候模型的另一个影响因素是云。

sentences.en: We usually associate hot summers with cloudless blue skies, but in fact clouds play a big part in the climate, as Kate Marvel explained to the BBC World Service.
sentences.zh: 我们通常把炎热的夏天与万里无云的蓝天联系在一起，但事实上，正如Kate Marvel向BBC世界服务部解释的那样，云在气候中扮演着重要角色。

sentences.en: So, the thing about clouds is that they have this dual effect.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于云的关键在于，它们具有这种双重效应。

sentences.en: They both cool the planet by blocking sunlight, and they warm the planet because they have their own greenhouse effect.
sentences.zh: 它们既通过阻挡阳光来冷却地球，又因为它们自身的温室效应而使地球变暖。

sentences.en: Right now, the unit that scientists use to measure the energy imbalance of the planet – how much it's out of whack – is Watts, like in a light bulb, per square metre.
sentences.zh: 目前，科学家用来测量地球能量不平衡的单位——即它失衡的程度——是瓦特，就像灯泡那样，每平方米。

sentences.en: Kate starts by saying, " The thing about clouds is." She uses the expression the thing about to introduce the most important detail about something.
sentences.zh: Kate首先说，“关于云的关键在于……”她使用“the thing about”这个表达来引入关于某事最重要的细节。

sentences.en: Here, that detail is that clouds both cool the planet by blocking sunlight but also warm it by trapping heat.
sentences.zh: 在这里，这个细节是云既能通过阻挡阳光冷却地球，也能通过困住热量使地球变暖。

sentences.en: So, climate models monitor clouds to accurately measure how much the Earth is out of whack.
sentences.zh: 因此，气候模型监测云层，以准确测量地球失衡的程度。

sentences.en: If something is out of whack, it's out of balance and not working properly.
sentences.zh: 如果某物“out of whack”，它就是失衡且运作不正常的。

sentences.en: Hmm. Climate models sound very complicated to me, Pippa.
sentences.zh: 嗯。对我来说，气候模型听起来非常复杂，Pippa。

sentences.en: For one thing, how can you monitor clouds which are constantly moving and changing?
sentences.zh: 一方面，你怎么能监测那些不断移动和变化的云呢？

sentences.en: Yeah. And how much information from around the world would the supercomputers need to make accurate projections?
sentences.zh: 是的。超级计算机需要来自世界各地的多少信息才能做出准确的预估？

sentences.en: It's a concern that BBC presenter Graihagh Jackson raised with Kate Marvel for BBC World Service programme The Climate Question.
sentences.zh: 这是BBC主持人Graihagh Jackson在BBC世界服务部节目《气候问题》中向Kate Marvel提出的一大担忧。

sentences.en: Surely we need to know the trajectory we're heading in, in order to adapt.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，为了适应气候变化，我们需要了解我们正朝着哪个轨迹前进。

sentences.en: Oh absolutely. You know, I am very pro- science.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是的。你知道的，我非常支持科学。

sentences.en: I am very pro- doing science because no climate change is unfortunately not on the table.
sentences.zh: 我非常支持进行科学研究，因为不幸的是，“没有气候变化”这种选项是不存在的。

sentences.en: Kate is very pro- science. If you're pro- something, it means you're in favour of it.
sentences.zh: Kate非常支持科学。如果你“pro-”某事，意味着你赞成它。

sentences.en: Models are complex, but they're necessary because unfortunately no climate change at all is not on the table, and that's an idiom, meaning it's not an option.
sentences.zh: 模型很复杂，但它们是必要的，因为不幸的是，完全没有气候变化是不可能的，这是一个习语，意思是不是一种选项。

sentences.en: If all this sounds a bit depressing. Kate's final message is more hopeful.
sentences.zh: 如果所有这些听起来有点让人沮丧，Kate的最后传达的信息则更有希望。

sentences.en: Climate models prove beyond doubt that the problem of global warming is created by humans, so we know beyond doubt that the solution is also in our hands.
sentences.zh: 气候模型毋庸置疑地证明了全球变暖的问题是由人类造成的，所以我们也毋庸置疑地知道，解决方案同样掌握在我们自己手中。

sentences.en: Now, Pippa, careful listeners might already know but go ahead and reveal the correct answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 现在，Pippa，仔细的听众可能已经知道了，不过请公布你问题的正确答案吧。

sentences.en: Yes. I asked you, "Which unit do scientists use to measure the Earth's energy imbalance?" And the answer was Watts per square metre.
sentences.zh: 好的。我问你：“科学家用哪个单位来测量地球的能量不平衡？”答案是每平方米瓦特。

sentences.en: And I didn't know that, Phil. Right, it's time to recap the vocabulary we heard during this programme.
sentences.zh: 我之前不知道这个，Phil。好了，是时候回顾我们在本节目中听到的词汇了。

sentences.en: A prediction is a statement about what you think will happen in the future.
sentences.zh: 预测（prediction）是关于你认为未来会发生什么陈述。

sentences.en: The adjective conditional means depending on other factors.
sentences.zh: 形容词“conditional”意为取决于其他因素。

sentences.en: You can use the informal expression the thing about to introduce the most important feature or detail of something.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用非正式表达“the thing about”来引入某事最重要的特征或细节。

sentences.en: The phrase out of whack means out of balance and not working properly.
sentences.zh: 短语“out of whack”意为失衡且运作不正常。

sentences.en: If you're pro- something, you're in favour of it.
sentences.zh: 如果你“pro-”某事，你就是赞成它。

sentences.en: And if something is not on the table, it's not an option.
sentences.zh: 如果某事“not on the table”，它就不是一个选项。

sentences.en: It's not available to us. That's the end of this episode of 6 Minute English.
sentences.zh: 它对我们来说不可行。6分钟英语本期节目到此结束。

sentences.en: Find a worksheet and quiz on our website to test what you've learned.
sentences.zh: 请在我们的网站上查找练习纸和测验，以测试你所学到的知识。

sentences.en: We'll be back next week with another episode, so make sure you don't miss it.
sentences.zh: 我们下周将推出另一期节目，千万不要错过。

sentences.en: Bye for now. Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见。拜拜！
